reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology combines rank centrality to infer relative skill levels from win-loss data, followed by kernel density estimation to reconstruct the full skill distribution. Rank centrality provides a stable, scalable estimator even under sparse data, while KDE allows for nonparametric inference of the underlying skill PDF. The negative entropy score serves as a robust metric for measuring competitiveness—low entropy implies narrow skill gaps and high predictability, whereas high entropy indicates broad skill diversity and unpredictability. This framework avoids direct estimation of individual skills, focusing instead on aggregate behavior. In GSE, these primitives enable simulation of realistic competition dynamics and adaptive strategy generation. In GSI, they support Bayesian inference on competitive balance and conformal prediction of future outcomes. The method’s strength lies in its ability to handle noisy, quantized data without requiring parametric assumptions, though it suffers from finite-sample bias and sensitivity to graph sparsity.
